showthatthedykesbecamemagnetizedsoonafterintrusion.Thepaleopoleisnotsignificantlydifferentfromthatobtainedfrom
the1759±1Mapost-orogenicJanLakeGranitefromtheHudsonianOrogeninsoutheastSaskatchewan.Thesepaleopolesfall
amongaclusterpreviouslydeterminedfrompost-orogenicoverprintsinawidevarietyofrocksandgeologicalsettingsacross
Laurentia.Theirmeanis20.8◦N,94.5◦W,A =5.2◦.Collectivelytheyrecordawidespreadremagnetizationepisodefollowing
95
the Hudsonian Orogeny, during which the polarity of the field remained constant. This single polarity interval (the Cleaver
Superchron)hasameanageofapproximately1747Ma,anditsdurationisatleast13millionyearsbutisprobablymuchlonger.
Withfurtherrefinement,itcouldbecomeaglobalstatigraphicalmarker.
Thereare18paleopolesfromredbedsandigneousrockswhichrecordthepaleofieldinwesternLaurentiamainlyoveran
extendedintervalweestimatetobeatleast100millionyearsbetweenabout1960and1830MaduringtheHudsonianOrogeny.
Overthisinterval,westernLaurentiaremainedatalowandessentiallyconstantlatitude.Reversalsofthegeomagneticfield
occurredopposedmagnetizationsbeingofapproximatelyequalfrequency;therearenumerousmagnetochronswhichcould,in
future,assistinregionalstratigraphiccorrelations.Onthebasisofsixstudies,weestimatethatthereferencepaleopoleforthis
intervalisat1.1◦S,71.7◦W,A =12.1◦ (N =6).Paleopolesfromtheother12studiesarespreadovera100◦ arcindicating
95
largevariablerotationsaboutlocalverticalaxeswhichprobablyresultedfromtranscurrentfaultingcausedbyindentationofthe
borderingArcheanSlaveandSuperiorcratonsduringtheHudsonianOrogeny.
These reference paleopoles show that during the Hudsonian Orogeny, western Laurentia was in paleolatitudes of 15–30◦.
During post-Hudsonian time (ca. 1750Ma) paleolatitudes were about 20◦ higher. Paleowind directions inferred by others,
indicatethatLaurentiaduringtheseintervalswasinthenorthernhemisphere.

leopoles and magnetizations. It is important to note
thatpost-HudsonianmagnetizationsoccuracrossLau-
rentia, but despite extensive study have not been ob-
served in the Grenville Province. Consequently, they
arelikelytohavebeenacquiredaftertheassemblyof

Because it overlies unconformably the Great Slave
Supergroup, it has been customary to consider that
their magnetizations was acquired at some signifi-
cantly later time than that of the Great Slave Super-
group(Reidetal.,1982;IrvingandMcGlynn,1981).
However,thereisnownogoodreasonforthis,itspa-
leopole falls on the same general arc as those from
other syn-Hudsonian sequences, and its paleolatitude
is similar (Fig. 12), so its age could fall in the above
wide range. That blocks of continental crust should
haveremainedlittlechangedinlatitudeoversuchlong
intervals is not unprecedented—Antarctica since the
EarlyCretaceous,forexample(Smithetal.,2000).

8. Reversals
As already noted all post-Hudsonian magnetiza-
tions represented in Fig. 11 have “normal” polarity,
theyoccuracrosstheLaurentiafromGreatBearLake
toGreenland(Fig.1).Somewereacquiredbyhematite
asitwasprecipitatedfrombasinalfluidsduringburial
diagenesis(AA;HS).Othersarecarriedbymagnetite
andwereprobablyacquiredasaresultofcoolingdur-
ingupliftfollowingmetamorphism(e.g.KA,KG,MD,
NA).Yetothers(CD,JL)probablywereacquireddur-
ing cooling following igneous crystallization. These
differentprocessesmayhaveoperatedatthesametime
somewhere across Laurentia, but it is highly unlikely
thattherecordofthem,obtainedbysuchahaphazard
sampling of such diverse rocks and settings, would
span only a brief interval. Also, the dates of the Jan
Lake Granite and the Cleaver Dykes are significantly
different,buttheirpaleopolesandpolarityareinagree-
ment. Therefore, we argue that the post-Hudsonian
